chunks: And ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa, from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Umar, from his father, from his grandfather, from ‘Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
The Euphrates is the master of the waters in this world and in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of the Euphrates River in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh transmits this chain from Imam Ali (AS) to elevate the Euphrates (Al-Furat) as the 'master of waters,' a title reflecting its dual role in physical purity and eschatological significance. This designation underscores the river's unique status in Shia hydro-theology, where its waters are not merely physical resources but vessels of spiritual merit, linking the believer's daily rituals to the cosmic order of the Hereafter.
